q: When a magnetised steel bar is cut into smaller pieces, every piece is a magnet with a(n) _____ and $S$-pole.
e: When a magnetised steel bar is cut into smaller pieces, every piece is a magnet with a(n) $N$-pole and $S$-pole. Every magnet has a north pole and a south pole, and like poles push apart.

q: A magnetised bar is composed of tiny magnets all lined up with their $N$-poles pointing in the _____.
e: A magnetised bar is composed of tiny magnets all lined up with their $N$-poles pointing in the same direction. Same direction here means lined up together, which is how a bar becomes magnetised. Random direction: pointing every which way, so the tiny magnets cancel.

q: In an unmagnetised bar, the 'tiny' magnets point in a _____ direction.
e: In an unmagnetised bar, the 'tiny' magnets point in a random direction. Random here means pointing every which way, so the tiny magnets cancel.

q: In an unmagnetised bar, the resulting magnetic effect of all the tiny magnets is _____ out.
e: In an unmagnetised bar, the resulting magnetic effect of all the tiny magnets is cancelled out. Cancelled here means the tiny magnets point randomly, so the bar has no net pole.
